newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BUX,futures rise, market waits MOL news.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BUX,futures rise, market waits MOL news.

text.p: The Budapest bourse moved a little higher on Monday as the market's sentiment turned more positive despite the fact that the dollar remained soft and that investors wait for MOL's new issue, traders said.
"The market's sentiment has improved from late last week," said Kalman Schuszter of New York Broker Budapest.
The BUX index finished at 5,560.26 points, up 49.90.
BUX futures firmed rose for the five nearest maturities by 30.00 to 69.00 points, but eased by 15.00 points for December 1998. March 1997 firmed 60.00 points to close at 5,675.

Nevertheless, traders doubted that in the near future the market would see hot days similar to those in January and earlier this month as investors seem to withhold their activities waiting for the issue of oil company MOL shares.
"MOL broke 3,100 forints...but I think it will rise substantially only when details of the planned issue come to the market," Schuszter said.
The planned new phase of MOL's privatisation keeps the market on its toes as it awaits details of its timing, pricing and offer size. MOL closed at 3,085 forints, up 20.
Smaller investor activity because expectations of MOL left it impact on the market, traders said.
"MOL shows direction to the market and until any details come out no major change could be expected," Schuszter said.

The market is focusing on a new MOL issue but two other companies, agricultural machinery Mezogep Rt and curtain maker Gardenia Rt were also planning share issue and both of them have already lodged their requests for bourse listing.
On Monday shares closed mixed within different sectors.
Within the chemicals, Borsodchem eased 15 forints to end at 6,280, while TVK fimed 50 forints to finish at 2,265.
In the pharmaceuticals sector Richter rose 100 forints to 12,600, Human closed steady at 3,200, while Egis eased 45 forints to end at 11,350.
However, Egis touched a session low of 11,000 forints on what traders said was still due to a 'sell' rating by ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett late Thursday.
In the hotel sector, Danubius rose three percent to close at 5,415, while Eravis dropped 50 to 4,700.
In the banking sector OTP finished steady at 3,950 forints, while Inter-Europa Bank touched higher by 50 forints to end at 50,000.
